scope:
Feature branch vs main: git diff origin/main...HEAD at 2224bf5 (code head 9b9eb81). Read mvp_compliance/management.py, models.py, admin.py, apps.py, exceptions.py, demo/settings.py, demo/management/commands/seed_demo.py, every added test, docs/models.md ('Declaring documents', 'When the slug is fixed'), docs/pages.md, ADR 0019, ADR 0026, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, research.md 'What already exists' and the design review's answers. Correctness and spec-compliance lens together.

ORCHESTRATOR QUESTION.
(1) Callers searched across Python, templates, docs and fixtures. Document.save(): 1 non-test caller that writes (seed_demo.py:524, update_fields=['kind'], never the slug), the admin change view through ModelAdmin.save_model, and 31 test call sites. None renames a declared slug outside the lock's own tests. DocumentQuerySet.update(): 2 non-test callers (seed_demo.py:398 and 403, filtered by name, writing kind and enforced, never the slug) and models.py:671 (that is VersionQuerySet, not this one), plus 22 test call sites; the only ones passing slug are the lock tests. bulk_update(): 0 non-test callers, 4 test call sites. DocumentAdmin.get_readonly_fields(): 1 caller in the repo (admin.py:54, get_prepopulated_fields, which drops the prepopulation when the slug is read-only, so a declared document's change form does not raise KeyError) plus Django's change view. declared_documents(): 4 callers (admin.py:43, models.py:78, models.py:271, management.py:88), all reading the setting at call time. seed_demo: finds documents by name with get_or_create, so it reaches the declared documents migrate created, and its slugs (seed_demo.py:176-186) match demo/settings.py. 0 stale references.
(2) Migrate twice on a copy of demo.sqlite3 (seeded): 'No migrations to apply' both times, 9 documents, 52 versions, 81 acceptances, every name, kind and enforcement unchanged. Migrate twice on a fresh database: the three declared documents created once with no version, kind 'agreed', enforced; the second run changed nothing. seed_demo on that fresh database then seeded all nine, the Impressum ending as a notice with one version in force; a second seed_demo and a third migrate changed nothing.
(3) A faulty declaration (fresh copy, LANGUAGE_CODE='de'): migrate raised ImproperlyConfigured in English naming every fault by slug (capital, reserved slug, a name held by 'terms-of-use', a name held by 'impressum-old', leading space, two declarations sharing a name, empty name) and wrote no document. Fixing the setting and migrating again created the missing ones, as docs/models.md says.
(4) The docs/models.md examples, run line by line against the branch: save() with a new slug on a declared document raises DeclaredDocumentError and the stored slug stays; update(slug=<same value>) and bulk_update([...], ['slug']) are refused, as documented ('refuse any slug value, including the one it already has'); name, kind and enforcement change through save(), save(update_fields=...) and update(); with the declaration removed the slug changes again, and after a publication PublishedVersionError is raised. Every import resolves and every name exists.
(5) The suite: 755 passed on the branch as configured. Run with tests.settings plus the demo's three declarations: 48 failed and 23 errored, every one a UNIQUE constraint on name or slug, or a get() finding the declared rows. That is FR-010 working as specified, and it is the consumer-facing gap in DOC-001.

Tests swept: 42 added or changed (test_management 22 including 5 parametrised, test_models 12, test_admin 3, test_app 1, test_exceptions 2, plus the 2 existing exception-set tests). None of the shapes that cannot fail. Mutations reasoned: dropping the existence filter makes test_a_second_call_creates_nothing raise IntegrityError; dropping the strip check fails the leading-space and trailing-space cases (Field.clean does not strip); dropping the declared branch in update() fails test_update_refuses_a_new_slug_and_leaves_the_stored_slug and the queryset-holding-any test; dropping the admin's declared condition makes the POST test reach save() and raise DeclaredDocumentError instead of 302; disconnecting the receiver fails tests/test_app.py. Known and accepted, not re-raised: the router-refusal branch has no test, non-string names raise Python's own error, bulk_create(update_conflicts=True) is documented as unguarded.

Django gates: no migration added; every new user-facing string goes through gettext or gettext_lazy and is in the .po file; no new model field; the new module follows django/contrib/sites/management.py's shape.

findings.claim: Nothing tells a consumer that declaring a document puts it in every test database, and in the database a fixture loads into, so their existing tests and fixtures that create a document with a declared slug or name stop working. The README and docs/models.md show exactly that create call next to the declaration.
findings.evidence: docs/models.md:121-160 ('Declaring documents') says only that the documents 'exist in every environment'. README.md:240 shows Document.objects.create(name="Privacy policy", slug="privacy-policy") and README.md:247-251 then suggests declaring {"privacy-policy": "Privacy policy"}, and docs/models.md:15 does the same. Once both are in place, that create raises IntegrityError (UNIQUE constraint failed: mvp_compliance_document.name), because migrate has already created the row (mvp_compliance/management.py:106-108; test database creation calls migrate). The same happens to a factory or a loaddata fixture that uses a declared slug or name, and a test that counts documents now counts the declared ones too. The changelog entry (CHANGELOG.md:12-20) and ADR 0026 do not mention it either.
findings.reproduction: Settings module importing tests.settings and adding MVP_COMPLIANCE_DOCUMENTS = {"privacy-policy": "Privacy policy", "terms-of-use": "Terms of use", "impressum": "Impressum"}; uv run pytest --ds=<that module>: 48 failed, 23 errors, every one a UNIQUE constraint on name or slug, or MultipleObjectsReturned from a get() that now finds the declared rows (for example tests/test_models.py::TestDocument::test_duplicate_name_is_refused, tests/test_migrations.py::TestEnforcedColumn).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short paragraph to docs/models.md 'Declaring documents', and one clause to the changelog entry: declared documents exist in the test database too, so a test fetches one with Document.objects.get(slug=...) rather than creating it, and a factory or fixture must not reuse a declared slug or name. In README.md, say the create call and the declaration are alternatives for the same document, not steps to combine.

notes: docs/models.md says a declaration is refused for 'a name with a space at either end' as one 'the admin would refuse'; the admin strips the spaces rather than refusing them. The behaviour is right, only the comparison is loose.

On a database with a case-insensitive collation (MySQL's default), a declared name differing only in case from an existing one passes the name check and fails inside the atomic block with IntegrityError instead of ImproperlyConfigured. Nothing is written either way; no current consumer runs MySQL.
